title: Speculative routes out of the solar system

title: Mass media and intellectual diversity

title: Argument over MacBook hardware choices

title: Ranking startup finalists by market fit

title: Proposal to end federal student loans
why: Policy opinion on student lending and bankruptcy dischargeability, without empirical support.

title: Developers, engineers and computer scientists differ in priorities
why: Developers ship duct-tape solutions, engineers build scalable systems, computer scientists chase theory; Google and Facebook cultures differ accordingly.

title: Why Tesla's cameras fall short of human vision
why: 20/20 vision is about 1 arc-minute; 20/40 needs about 30 pixels per degree, and Tesla's forward cameras are compared against that.

title: Why instruments last longer than laptops
why: Wish about the durability of musical gear versus computers. Personal reflection with no technical mechanism.

title: Emergent harms of ad-funded social media
why: Essay-style commentary on Facebook's side effects. Opinion built on a quoted essay.

title: Weighing theories of COVID origins
why: Personal reasoning about four origin theories and government trust. Speculative, not a technical lesson.

title: Why incumbents' vertical integration beats cheap newcomers
why: Samsung and Apple control chips, antennas and cases, so undercutting on price is hard; newcomers need a distinct edge, not just lower cost.

title: Anecdote about dietary science shifts
why: Personal story and distrust of public health messaging. Opinion without a transferable lesson.

title: Who controls the Android experience
why: Opinion on carriers and manufacturers versus Apple. Argumentative, with no technical explanation.

title: Mosquitoes are the deadliest animal to humans
why: Mosquitoes cause about a million deaths a year, far more than snakes (50,000), dogs (25,000) or crocodiles (1,000).

title: Energy per capita shapes farming and fertility
why: Below about 1 MWh per capita, a country lacks nitrogen and steel production, so farming stays labor-heavy and families have more children.

title: Arbitrary symbols and how math is taught
why: Opinion on teaching math through exploration and on mathematicians' notation. Argumentative, not a concrete explanation.

title: Budgeting for an ergonomic workstation
why: Spend most on an adjustable chair and a good keyboard, since they last years; cheap stretches and habits cover the rest.

title: Debate over unsafe code in Rust crates
why: Back-and-forth over how common bad unsafe usage is in crates. Argumentative, with anecdotal data.

title: Evolved programs game badly designed fitness functions
why: Evolving systems exploited timing side channels and scheduler communication to score well, so fitness functions must be designed against gaming.

title: Critique of computer science trivia interviews
why: Opinion that trivia interviews select for algorithm recall rather than shipping software. Argument, not a teaching point.

title: Why companies hesitate to hire junior developers
why: Training newcomers costs senior time, and trained developers leave for higher pay, so the hiring math rarely favors juniors.

title: Why companies hesitate to hire junior developers

title: Why Chennai's water crisis runs deeper than drought
why: Borewells mask the shortage for many households, while a leaky, unmetered pipe network and weak government ownership of water persist.

title: Race and university admissions argument
why: Political argument about affirmative action and Asian American applicants. Contested opinion, no technical lesson.

title: Rebuttal to 'don't learn to code'
why: Opinion that programming is logical thinking for everyone. Rhetorical argument rather than a technical explanation.

title: Shkreli arrest and harassment allegations
why: News commentary on a public figure's conduct. Gossip-style reporting with no technical lesson.

title: Opinion on the Starbucks card donation
why: Moral opinion about spending someone else's money in a social experiment. Argumentative.

title: Opinion on gender stereotypes and feminism
why: Personal opinion about gender roles and a Disney marketing controversy. Argumentative.

title: Why subsidizing demand raises college prices
why: Subsidies without matching supply growth push up prices: demand rises while the number of campuses and beds stays flat.

title: Union strategy and Tesla's workforce
why: Political argument that unions target competitors and use strikes for their own survival. Partisan opinion.

title: Argument for default DNS over HTTPS
why: Opinion defending Cloudflare DoH as a default against censorship. Argumentative, without new technical detail.

title: Tesla's Q3 discounts boosted profit
why: Enthusiast commentary on discounts that inflated quarterly sales. Speculative, with no verifiable mechanism.

title: Argument about plants and diet ethics
why: Opinion arguing that plants' signaling makes eating them ethically equivalent. Argumentative.

title: The Seattle Freeze explained
why: Personal social observations about locals versus transplants. Anecdotal, with no transferable lesson.

title: Personal account of self-taught CS study
why: Long personal narrative about being unprepared at Cambridge. Anecdote without a clear lesson.

title: Spotting weak evidence in an alcohol treatment study
why: One significant result among many nulls, pooled from two trials and uncorrected for multiple comparisons: a fragile finding despite 'high certainty' labels.

title: Opinion on when to use exceptions
why: Opinion that exceptions should be reserved for irreconcilable errors. Reasonable view, but not a substantive explanation.

title: How 1970s growth controls shaped Bay Area housing
why: Anti-growth court rulings, city caps like Petaluma's 1972 ordinance, and Prop 13 and rent control compounded into today's Bay Area housing shortage.

title: Critique of a job seeker's email style
why: Personal critique of a candidate's writing style and self-awareness. Ad hominem rather than a lesson.

title: Teaching data structures in Python instead of Java
why: Python lets courses skip Java generics and access modifiers, so students focus on structures, complexity and iterators before hand-compiling to MIPS.

title: Founder's account of refusing unethical data deals
why: Personal ethics story about declining surveillance-style data requests. Anecdotal, with no technical lesson.

title: Whisper transcribes and translates French on a GPU
why: Whisper ran about 17x real time on an RTX 3090, detected French automatically, and gave good but imperfect transcripts and translations.

title: Practical security habits for production services
why: Dry-run platform updates, track dependency fixes, and run known-good source builds; input validation alone has bought little real security.

title: Why Apple's phone chips rival desktop single-core speed
why: The A13 matches top desktop single-core scores at about 5 watts, though phones cannot sustain that in bursts, so larger devices could go further.

title: Founder's story of leaving hardware for software
why: Personal account of regulatory and manufacturing pain. Anecdotal, with no transferable mechanism.

title: How Reddit subreddit ad targeting works
why: Subreddit targeting reaches subscribers and recent visitors to a subreddit or its posts; the change came with the new ads platform.

title: Opinion on what recommendations should do
why: User preference for surprising recommendations over more of the same. Opinion, not an explanation of how systems work.

title: Anecdotes about neighborhood app racism
why: Anecdotes and opinion about discriminatory posts and weak privacy. Argumentative with no technical lesson.

title: Practical gotchas for moving to Canada
why: Immigration consultants exist for good reason: apply for health coverage immediately on arrival, and expect to rebuild banking and credit history from scratch.

title: Why Linux GUI toolkits seem fragmented
why: Most drivers ship in the kernel, but GTK and Qt break compatibility across versions, unlike Win32's decades of binary compatibility.

title: Why faces cannot reliably reveal emotions
why: Emotions unfold over time, use the whole body, overlap heavily in expression, and are culturally modulated, so single-frame classifiers face a hard ceiling.

title: Svelte versus React opinion
why: Subjective praise for Svelte's docs and React's churn. Opinion, with no concrete technical explanation.

title: How Amazon's calibration pressures managers into attrition
why: Written policy is fair, but managers face yearly quotas for performance plans, so the lowest-rated staff are pushed out.

title: Debate over fighter jets and rifles
why: Argument about whether advanced aircraft are worth it versus simpler ground weapons. Opinion, not a technical lesson.

title: Opinion against on-device CSAM scanning
why: Privacy advocacy against Apple's scanning plan. Argument and opinion, without new technical detail.

title: Quant traders versus engineers in high-frequency trading
why: Traders earn a share of profits and need steady psychology, while non-trading engineers earn salaries; the roles differ sharply.

title: Opinion linking ADHD diagnoses to parenting
why: Anecdotal claim that diagnoses reflect lifestyle and parenting. Unsupported opinion.

title: Why signed overflow UB enables loop optimizations
why: Assuming signed overflow never happens lets compilers unroll loops and precompute bounds; wrapping semantics would block many optimizations.

title: Opinion on visual tools and complexity
why: Cultural opinion on Visual Basic-style tools versus expert tooling. Argumentative, with a brief point about abstraction.

title: Why apps probably aren't secretly recording you
why: Continuous speech recognition would consume noticeable CPU and bandwidth, iOS shows mic indicators, and traffic analysis would expose it; coincidence explains most cases.

title: OK-Cancel versus Cancel-OK button order
why: Opinion that either order works if it is consistent. Reasonable, but mostly a matter of preference.

title: Opinion on UFO sightings and religion
why: Speculation about conspiracy beliefs and the Dyson swarm. Opinion without new evidence.

title: Opinion on gender wages and college
why: Political argument about education gaps and sexism. Contested opinion with no technical lesson.

title: Measuring ripgrep against GNU grep fairly
why: With equal parallelism and file coverage, ripgrep is about 2x faster than GNU grep; bigger gaps mostly come from default filtering or Unicode.

title: Moderation options and Section 230
why: Frames three moderation models and argues for retroactive moderation. Policy argument rather than a neutral explanation.

title: Polished how-to videos are often less accurate
why: A finish carpenter found polished how-to videos often less accurate than shaky jobsite clips; judge expertise, not production quality.

title: Personal struggles with sleep and focus
why: Personal account of sleep problems and late-night work. Anecdotal, with no transferable mechanism.

title: Why USPS delays come from the flats collapse
why: COVID collapsed letter and magazine volume while packages surged; flats sorters cannot handle packages, so USPS shut them down and cut overtime.

title: Reply on finding paying problems
why: Reply to a specific post with motivational advice. Only makes sense in context.

title: Why 21700 cells may trade power for capacity
why: Larger cells have lower power density for the same weight, so Tesla must cut performance draw or add cells and weight.

title: Filming police: party versus bystander rules
why: Parties to an interaction may film closely; bystanders can be asked to stay about 8 feet away, a buffer courts already upheld.

title: Personal account of living in the UK
why: Lifestyle account of remote consulting from the UK. Personal, with no broad technical lesson.

title: Argument against romantic love
why: Opinion that romance is a delusion driven by looks. Argumentative and unsupported.

title: Predictions about Starship delays
why: Forecast of schedule delays and comparison with other rockets. Speculative opinion.

title: Complaints about Intel Mac external displays
why: Enthusiastic comparison of Apple laptops with personal complaints about throttling. Anecdotal and partisan.

title: Why defer breaks when cleanup is refactored
why: Scope-based defer runs cleanup when the creating function returns, so moving creation into helpers breaks; value-based destructors travel with the object.

title: Opinion on the diversity pendulum
why: Personal grievance and prediction about diversity movements swinging back. Argumentative.

title: Brazilian protests and government corruption
why: Political account of protests and taxes from a citizen abroad. Opinion, not a technical lesson.

title: Why bright indoor light needs an evening cutoff
why: Clocks handle photoperiods of about 14-15 hours; 18 hours under bright light lengthens the internal day and cuts sleep, so evening dimming matters.

title: Critique of WWI comparisons to today
why: Historical argument about WWI causes and modern parallels. Opinion, with some contested claims.

title: How fiber taps evade OTDR fault detection
why: A small beam splitter diverts photons without a break, while cutting the fiber triggers OTDR repair alerts, so taps must avoid a detectable fault.

title: Complaint about Gmail sign-in verification
why: Account of a confusing verification flow and an incognito workaround. Complaint rather than a transferable lesson.

title: Idea for a 25-friend social feed
why: Product idea limiting feeds to 25 friends, with an unsourced claim about harms. Opinion, not evidence.

title: Why EV regenerative braking weakens in the cold
why: Cold batteries accept less regenerative charge, so single-pedal braking fades in freezing weather, which is a practical EV driving fact.

title: Advice on social skills at parties
why: Opinion that social skills matter more than reading. Advice without concrete technical content.

title: Moderator note on downweighting comments
why: Moderation notice about community downweighting and YC stories. Meta-discussion, not a technical lesson.

title: Skepticism about singularity predictions
why: Opinion that singularity talk is a cargo cult. Argumentative, with no concrete evidence.

title: Anecdote on degrees and job requirements
why: Personal story about hiring credentials versus actual job demands. Anecdotal with no transferable lesson.

title: Opinion against global competitive ladders
why: Game designer's opinion that global ranking hinges on unrealistic anti-cheat and encourages toxic play. Opinion-driven.

title: Why lenses cannot heat past the source temperature
why: A lens cannot heat a target above the radiation source's temperature; moonlight is reflected sunlight, so the Moon's own temperature is irrelevant.

title: Defense of obvious code comments
why: Opinion that comments help newcomers. Reasonable but argumentative, with no new technical mechanism.

title: How a bad kernel driver bricked cloud nodes
why: A bad driver update caused boot loops; recovery meant detaching each cloud disk, deleting the .sys file on another node, and reattaching, straining storage.

title: Commentary on Assange's bail breach
why: News commentary quoting a critic on Swedish charges. Political and legal debate, not a technical lesson.

title: Wish for assistant-driven desktop interfaces
why: Speculative wish for AI-driven file management instead of folders. Opinion without a concrete design.

title: Confusing electrode conventions in tDCS research
why: tDCS studies label electrodes active and reference, obscuring which side gets anodal stimulation; a DIY LM317 current limiter costs about $30.

title: Personal account of disability and welfare
why: Personal story about being denied disability support and comparing systems. Anecdote and political opinion.
